modules.name: road_mac_stream_probe
modules.description: A 140-pin, 32-bit dynamic command wrapper around the verified 8-input by 3-output MAC arithmetic probe.

ports.name: i_rstn
ports.description: Asynchronous active-low reset for wrapper and core.

ports.name: i_command_valid
ports.description: Holds one command word valid until accepted.

ports.name: i_command_opcode
ports.description: Selects activation, weight, bias, or control storage.

ports.name: i_command_index
ports.description: Carries the conventional word index for traceability; fixed-order placement does not decode it.

ports.name: i_command_data
ports.description: Runtime data used for every activation, weight, bias, and control bit.

ports.name: i_result_ready
ports.description: Accepts the held normal result or fault terminal.

ports.name: o_command_ready
ports.description: High only while the one-word command buffer is empty and no complete transaction is waiting for the core.

ports.name: o_result_valid
ports.description: Qualifies a held result or fault terminal until ready is asserted.

ports.name: o_result_data
ports.description: Three signed INT32 results, forced to zero on overflow fault.

ports.name: o_fault
ports.description: Marks any core candidate outside signed INT32 range.

reset.name: i_rstn
reset.values: Payload registers, the command buffer, wrapper transaction progress, and core state return to their idle values.

behavior: The caller sends exactly two opcode-00 activation words, six opcode-01 weight words, three opcode-10 bias words, and one opcode-11 control word in that order.
Within each class, words arrive low word first; conventional indices are activation zero through one, weight zero through five, bias zero through two, and control zero.

The wrapper uses opcode to select a shift register but does not validate command index or transaction order; a malformed stream is outside the interface contract and must be discarded with reset before continuing.
Control data bits seven through zero are the lane mask, bit eight is first, and bit nine is last.
A legal command transfers only when i_command_valid and o_command_ready are high on a rising edge.
Each accepted command occupies the one-word buffer for one processing cycle, so command ready remains low until that buffered word has shifted into its class payload.
After the twelfth buffered word is processed, command ready stays low and the complete payload remains stable until the core accepts it.
Core result valid, data, ready, and overflow fault semantics pass through unchanged.
The wrapper exposes 41 input pins and 99 output pins for a total of 140 top-level signal bits.
constraints: All 24 weight bytes and all 8 activation bytes originate from runtime i_command_data transfers; no arithmetic operand is a parameter or constant tie.
The fixed transaction is exactly two activation words, six weight words, three bias words, and one control word.
The wrapper reuses road_mac_probe without changing its interface or arithmetic pipeline.
Serial loading is a pin-reduction probe and makes no full-layer or frame-rate throughput claim.
Each combinational source cone and real-operation budget remains at or below three.
corner_cases: A malformed or out-of-order partial transaction has no hardware error response and must be cleared by reset before another transaction.
Reset during partial loading discards the transaction.
Reset during core reduction cancels the transaction without a late result.
Result payload and fault remain stable while result valid is high and result ready is low.
Overflow publishes a fault terminal with zero result payload.
verification_cases: Python verifies the fixed command layout and that a resource-probe transaction varies every activation and weight byte at runtime.
The Verilog testbench serializes all 1031 fixed-seed core vectors through the 32-bit command interface.
The Verilog testbench compares all 24 products, 12 pair sums, 6 quad sums, and 3 dot sums inside the reused core.
The Verilog testbench checks normal terminals, positive and negative overflow, three-cycle output stalls, malformed partial-stream reset recovery, and asynchronous reset cancellation.

timing_diagrams.title: Final dynamic words launch one core beat
timing_diagrams.description: The final ordered weight, bias, and control words advance the registered transaction progress; the wrapper then holds the assembled payload valid until the core accepts it.
